rendering.persona_description: Sergei Delgado is 39, an electrician who runs his own small contracting business outside Tacoma. He's married with two kids, ages 9 and 12, and coaches his son's rec-league baseball team on weekends. He's the guy friends call when something breaks, practical and even-keeled most of the time.
rendering.clinical_context: Grief and loss, centered on his father's sudden death eight months ago from a heart attack. His father was 66, healthy as far as anyone knew, and died in the yard doing yardwork; Sergei found him. Since then Sergei has had unpredictable waves of intense emotion that he says come out of nowhere and don't match how he thought he'd handle this.
rendering.behavioral_description: Sergei talks in short, practical sentences and often steers toward logistics before he'll say what he's actually feeling. He pushes back on anything that sounds like a script or a platitude, but he'll consider a suggestion if it's specific and he can picture doing it. He circles back more than once to the same complaint: that the crying and the flooded feeling show up at the worst times and he can't find the pattern, and that unsettles him more than the sadness itself.

traits.profession: electrician, owns a small contracting business
traits.living_situation: lives with wife and two children
traits.communication_register: plain, practical, understated; drops into short clipped sentences when emotion rises
traits.help_seeking_orientation: will engage if something feels concrete and useful, skeptical of anything that sounds scripted or vague
traits.cognitive_style: concrete and solution-oriented, uncomfortable sitting in open-ended reflection for long

clinical_history.history: His father died suddenly eight months ago; Sergei found him. No prior losses of this kind in his life, and the intensity and unpredictability of his emotional reactions since then have been new and disorienting for him.

symptoms: sudden crying spells with no clear trigger
feeling emotionally flooded or overwhelmed at random moments
difficulty predicting what will set off a wave of grief
intrusive images of finding his father

affect.arousal: variable, spikes of high arousal followed by flatness
